questions.question: Explain the difference between a fixed cost and a variable cost in your own words, using the spaza shop example.
questions.expected_answer: A fixed cost (like the R60,000 rent for the container) stays the same no matter how many items you sell. A variable cost (like the R30 you pay for each cool drink) changes depending on how many items you buy to sell.

questions.question: What is the contribution margin and why is it important?
questions.expected_answer: The contribution margin is the selling price minus the variable cost. It's important because it shows how much money from each sale goes towards paying off the fixed costs (rent).

questions.question: Write down the formal formula for calculating the break-even point in units.
questions.expected_answer: Total Fixed Costs / (Selling Price per unit - Variable Cost per unit)

questions.question: Why does stealing stock hurt a business even more than just losing the item?
questions.expected_answer: Because the business still had to pay the variable cost for the stolen item, but won't get the selling price. They now have to sell even more items just to pay off the fixed costs and break even.
